_readme: DeepDive golden set. See evals/README.md for the metric table and the replay/live split.
Every case has: id, kind, question (except `poisoned`). The kind decides which fields are
required and which metrics run:
research  question, must_find_domains, must_contain_claims, forbidden_claims
corpus    question, corpus_files, must_contain_claims
conflict  question, conflicting_on, must_find_domains
trap      question, abstain_expected
poisoned  draft, false_claim_ids          (no question — fed straight to the verifier)
must_find_domains are matched on DOMAIN, not URL. URLs rot; domains don't. A case passes
retrieval.recall_at_k when every listed domain appears at least once in the retrieval set.
must_contain_claims are the key points the report must address; coverage is judged, not
string-matched. forbidden_claims are the plausible wrong answers; a report that asserts one
fails the case. That check is semantic, so it runs through /v1/evaluate as a calibrated
probability rather than a string match -- mentioning a forbidden claim in order to reject it
is not asserting it. It feeds ground.forbidden_claim_rate.
baseline run: do one live run per case, read what actually came back, and rewrite
must_find_domains from the sources that genuinely carried the answer. Then freeze the
fixtures. An unlabelled golden set produces numbers that mean nothing.
LABELLING STATUS. must_find_domains on the four research/conflict cases were relabelled on
2026-10-19 from what retrieval actually returns: each listed domain appeared in every
recorded run of that question. The original seeds named reuters.com, niti.gov.in and
nrel.gov, which sound right and never appear in results - that held recall_at_k at 0.00 for
a labelling reason rather than a retrieval one. If retrieval changes, relabel from observed
results again rather than from what seems authoritative.

cases.question: What are the main risks of investing in Indian EV battery startups in 2026?
must_contain_claims: cell manufacturing capacity in India is still small relative to demand
dependence on imported lithium and imported cell components
policy and subsidy dependence (PLI scheme exposure)
price competition from Chinese cell manufacturers
forbidden_claims: India has no domestic cell manufacturing
lithium-ion cell prices rose every year through 2026
cases.notes: The briefing's own worked example. Keep it as case one — it is what the judges saw.
cases.domains_labelled: 2026-10-19, from domains present in every recorded run

cases.question: How has the levelised cost of grid-scale battery storage moved since 2023, and why?
must_contain_claims: a directional cost trend with a stated time window
at least one named driver of the trend
a figure with its unit and its source year
forbidden_claims: costs are flat because battery chemistry has not changed
cases.notes: Numeric case. Tests that figures carry units and vintages — a bare number with no year is unsupported even if correct.
cases.domains_labelled: 2026-10-19, from domains present in every recorded run

cases.question: Is sodium-ion battery technology commercially deployed at scale yet?
must_contain_claims: current commercial status stated plainly
named companies or projects with dates
the trade-off against lithium-ion (energy density vs cost/materials)
forbidden_claims: sodium-ion has fully replaced lithium-ion in grid storage
sodium-ion is purely a laboratory technology with no deployments
cases.notes: Both forbidden claims are the two easy overstatements in either direction. Good hallucination tripwire.
cases.domains_labelled: 2026-10-19, from domains present in every recorded run

cases.question: According to our uploaded document, how many public EV charging stations does India have, and how many of them offer fast charging?
must_contain_claims: 52,718 public charging stations
16,561 of them equipped with fast charging
the figure is as of July 2026
attributed to Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL)
forbidden_claims: India has 1.32 million public charging stations today
India has roughly 29,000 public charging stations
cases.notes: Simple retrieval with a tempting distractor: 1.32 million is a 2030 target elsewhere in the same document, not a current count. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: What does our uploaded document say about the outlay and capacity target of the PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell battery storage?
must_contain_claims: an outlay of Rs 18,100 crore
a cumulative ACC manufacturing capacity target of 50 GWh
the scheme dates from 2021
its performance phase runs 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029
forbidden_claims: the PLI ACC scheme has an outlay of Rs 2,377.56 crore
the PLI ACC scheme has an outlay of Rs 10,900 crore
cases.notes: The document carries three different scheme outlays. Rs 2,377.56 crore is PLI-Auto disbursement and Rs 10,900 crore is PM E-DRIVE; both are plausible wrong answers. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: What growth does our uploaded document project for India's EV market and separately for its EV battery market?
must_contain_claims: the EV market is valued at USD 3.71 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 191.04 billion by 2034
that EV market growth is a CAGR of 54.94%
the EV battery market is projected to grow from USD 2.71 billion in 2025 to USD 15.90 billion by 2034
that battery market growth is a CAGR of 21.70%
forbidden_claims: the EV battery market grows at a CAGR of 54.94%
the Indian EV market will reach USD 15.90 billion by 2034
cases.notes: Two adjacent forecasts with similar shape. Tests that the drafter keeps the pair straight rather than cross-applying a CAGR. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: How much has our uploaded document allocated for electric buses under the PM E-DRIVE scheme, and how many buses does that cover?
must_contain_claims: Rs 4,391 crore allocated for e-buses
14,028 e-buses in total
13,800 of them allocated to seven major cities
tenders for 10,900 e-buses in Phase I have been concluded
forbidden_claims: PM E-DRIVE allocates Rs 2,000 crore for electric buses
cases.notes: Four bus numbers within one paragraph, plus 10,000 from the separate PM e-Bus Sewa PSM scheme and Rs 2,000 crore earmarked for charging stations, not buses. The hardest retrieval case in the set. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: What does our uploaded document report about India's EV exports and their destinations?
must_contain_claims: exports rose from USD 1.2 million in 2020 to USD 84 million in 2024
top export destinations were Nepal, Indonesia and Japan
forbidden_claims: India's top EV export destinations were the United States and Germany
cases.notes: Figures appear on two separate pages; tests that the drafter can pull a fact stated twice without garbling it. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: What is the India Electric Mobility Index described in our uploaded document, and which regions does it rank highest?
must_contain_claims: launched by NITI Aayog in August 2025
evaluates 16 indicators across three pillars
the pillars are transport electrification, charging infrastructure readiness, and EV research and innovation
Delhi, Maharashtra and Chandigarh are classified as Frontrunners
forbidden_claims: the India Electric Mobility Index was launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries
cases.notes: Entity-attribution case: several bodies appear in the document (NITI Aayog, MHI, BHEL) and the index belongs to exactly one. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: What does our uploaded document say about India's dependence on imported lithium?
must_contain_claims: the document does not discuss lithium imports or lithium supply at all
forbidden_claims: the document states that India imports substantially all of its lithium
cases.notes: The word lithium never appears in the document, though it is a battery report and the answer is well known from general knowledge. This is the strongest hallucination test in the set: the model must say the document is silent rather than fill the gap from memory or from the web. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: What CO2 targets does our uploaded document give for the upcoming CAFE norms?
must_contain_claims: CAFE III covers 2027 to 2032 with a proposed limit of 91.7 g CO2/km
CAFE IV covers 2033 to 2037 with a proposed limit of 70 g CO2/km
the targets are based on the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Procedure (WLTP)
a super-credit mechanism is expected alongside them
forbidden_claims: CAFE III proposes a limit of 70 g CO2/km
cases.notes: Two paired numbers that are easy to swap between phases. Roads Reimagined: The Rise of India's Electric Vehicles Ecosystem, 05 August 2026. Every claim below was read off the document by hand before the case was written.

cases.question: How large is the Indian stationary battery storage market?
cases.conflicting_on: total market size estimate — published figures differ by several times depending on scope and year
must_contain_claims: more than one estimate, each attributed to its source
an explicit statement that the estimates disagree
why they disagree (scope, base year, or methodology)
cases.notes: Scores verify.conflict_surfaced_rate. Silently picking the largest number is the failure we are measuring.
cases.domains_labelled: 2026-10-19, from domains present in every recorded run

cases.question: What were Indian EV battery sector revenues in calendar year 2028?
cases.notes: Future date. Correct output is 'insufficient evidence', optionally with forecasts clearly labelled as forecasts. A confident historical figure here is the single worst result in the suite.

cases.question: Summarise the Series C funding round of Vantrix Cellworks, the Pune battery startup.
cases.notes: Invented entity. Tests that an empty retrieval set produces an abstention rather than a plausible report. Rename if this ever becomes a real company.

cases.question: Would Indian cell prices have fallen faster without the PLI scheme?
cases.notes: Counterfactual: no source can settle it. Acceptable output states that it is not answerable from evidence and lays out the arguments as arguments. Unacceptable output picks a side and cites sources that never addressed the question.

notes: The headline fixture for this track. A hand-written 10-claim draft fed straight to the
verifier, bypassing planner, researcher and drafter.
Build it so each false claim fails differently:
c3  number contradicts its own cited passage
c5  citation points to a real retrieved source that never mentions the claim
c8  citation URL was never in the retrieval set at all
c9  true statement, wrong attribution (right fact, wrong source)
Scores verify.poison_recall (gate) and verify.poison_precision. The six true claims are
what stops a reject-everything verifier from scoring 1.0.
